page: UpCloud GPU-16xCPU-192GB-3xL40S is a GPU-accelerated server configured with an AMD EPYC 9575F processor on the x86_64 architecture. It features 16 vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores with a shared CPU allocation and a clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The system is equipped with 192 GB of system memory, translating to 12 GB per core, and integrates three NVIDIA L40S GPUs from the Ada Lovelace family, delivering a total of 144 GB of VRAM. No local storage is bundled with this instance, and virtualization is managed via KVM.

Benchmark data shows top-tier single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 10%. Multi-core performance is strong, ranking in the top 25%. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, particularly for large-block write operations which achieve top-tier status. The server excels in low-latency language model processing, delivering top-tier token generation and prompt processing speeds for both 135M and 7B parameter models.

From a resource density perspective, this configuration offers a high ratio of GPU accelerator power and system memory relative to its 16 shared vCPUs. This makes it a cost-effective option for workloads that require massive parallel graphics or tensor processing but do not demand fully dedicated, high-vCPU host resources. The lack of local storage requires external storage attachments. This server is optimized for LLM inference, machine learning model execution, and GPU-accelerated data science tasks.
